facts.statement: The genus contains only one species, Scleromochlus taylori, which was named by Arthur Smith Woodward in 1907.
facts.quote: The genus contains the type and only species Scleromochlus taylori, named by Arthur Smith Woodward in 1907.

facts.statement: Fossils of Scleromochlus have been found in the Carnian Lossiemouth Sandstone of Scotland.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been found in the Carnian Lossiemouth Sandstone of Scotland.

facts.statement: Scleromochlus taylori was about 18.1 cm long and possessed long hind legs.
facts.quote: Scleromochlus taylori was about 18.1 cm long, with long hind legs; it may have been capable of four-legged and two-legged locomotion.

facts.statement: The phylogenetic position of Scleromochlus is debated, with analyses placing it as a basal ornithodiran, a sister-taxon to pterosaurs, or a basal avemetatarsalian outside Ornithodira.
facts.quote: A lightly built cursorial animal, its phylogenetic position has been debated; as different analyses have found it to be either the basal-most ornithodiran, the sister-taxon to Pterosauria, or a basal member of Avemetatarsalia that lies outside of Ornithodira.

facts.statement: Scleromochlus lived from the Carnian to the Norian stages, approximately 237 to 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Norian (237 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Scleromochlus is classified within the unranked order Ornithodira.
Scleromochlus is classified within the unranked family Pterosauromorpha.
Scleromochlus belongs to the family Scleromochlidae.
A 2022 interpretation based on a more complete analysis of known remains determined that Scleromochlus was a running animal, either quadrupedal or bipedal.
facts.quote: En una nueva interpretación de 2022, obtenida a partir de un análisis más completo de los restos conocidos, se determinó que Scleromochlus habría sido un animal corredor (cuadrúpedo o bípedo).

rejected.statement: Scleromochlus is an extinct genus of small pterosauromorph archosaurs named for its hard lever-like bones.
rejected.quote: Scleromochlus (from Greek, 'hard' and Greek, 'lever') is an extinct genus of small pterosauromorph archosaurs from the Late Triassic Lossiemouth Sandstone of Scotland.
